title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (2026)
summary: How to request medical records from Children's Hospital of Philadelphia in 2026: the MR-109 form, department contacts, fees, MyCHOP limits, and HIPAA rules.
body_markdown:
Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) is one of the country's largest pediatric health systems, with[724 beds in use](https://www.chop.edu/about-us/annual-report-of-our-financials/hospital-statistics) and more than 1.6 million outpatient visits in fiscal 2025. For personal injury attorneys handling cases involving minor patients, understanding CHOP's medical record request process is essential for timely case evaluation and demand package preparation. But manually requesting, tracking, and verifying records from a facility this size can eat up time that should go to case strategy. Codes Health offers AI-powered medical record retrieval that manages multi-channel provider outreach, catches authorization errors before they cause delays, and reports an average turnaround of a couple of weeks for complete records.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


CHOP uses its Authorization to Release/Obtain Patient Information form (MR-109) for standard authorization-based record requests, with special signature rules for mental health records.


-


Different departments handle different record types: Health Information Management (HIM) manages general records, while radiology and mental health have separate request processes.


-


CHOP doesn't promise immediate production, and turnaround varies by request. HIPAA's 30-day deadline applies to qualifying patient right-of-access requests, not to every attorney authorization request.


-


Pennsylvania's 2026 fee schedule caps search and retrieval at[$29.61](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/health/resources/medical-record-fees) , though that fee can't be charged when patients request their own records.


-


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of rejected requests and can lead to correction requests and delays.


-


Codes Health validates authorizations before submission, manages multi-channel provider outreach, and verifies record completeness before delivery.


## **Understanding Your Rights: How to Request Medical Records from CHOP**


### **Patient Portals: Your First Step to Online Access**


CHOP offers a patient portal called MyCHOP that provides access to portions of the electronic medical record. Through the portal, patients and guardians can view test results, immunization records, visit summaries, and some clinical notes. CHOP states that MyCHOP doesn't contain the complete medical record, which attorneys typically need for litigation.


Patients can also submit a medical record request through the MyCHOP questionnaire section. For legal professionals seeking comprehensive documentation, a formal authorization-based request is still the standard route.


### **HIPAA Requirements for Personal Record Requests**


HIPAA generally requires action within 30 calendar days on a qualifying patient right-of-access request, with one permitted 30-day extension with written notice. That deadline doesn't automatically apply to disclosures made under a HIPAA authorization, such as most attorney-initiated requests. HHS notes that an[authorization has no](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/why-depend-on-the-individuals-right/index.html) HIPAA timeliness requirement, unlike a right-of-access request.


CHOP doesn't publish a standard processing time for authorization-based requests and notes that records aren't immediately available because of request volume and compliance requirements, so turnaround varies by request.


For pediatric records, additional rules apply. Parents or legal guardians generally sign authorizations for patients under 18, and guardianship documentation should accompany the form if the signer isn't a parent. For mental health records, CHOP requires patients 14 or older to sign and initial the authorization themselves. Each of these requirements is another point where errors can delay a request.


## **Essential Forms for CHOP Medical Records: Release of Information and Authorization**


### **Downloading CHOP-Specific Authorization Forms**


CHOP uses a specific HIPAA authorization form for standard authorization-based record requests. The main forms include:


-


**English Version:**[Authorization to Release/Obtain](https://www.chop.edu/sites/default/files/about-us-HIPAA_Authorization.pdf) Patient Information (MR-109)


-


**Spanish Version:** HIPAA Authorization Form in Spanish


-


**Reproductive Health Attestation:** CHOP's website currently provides an attestation for certain requests. Because a federal court vacated most of the[federal reproductive health rule](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/reproductive-health/final-rule-fact-sheet/index.html) supporting that requirement in June 2025, confirm CHOP's current operational requirements before submitting one.


Some outpatient, specialty care, and primary care requests are routed directly to the department where care took place.


### **Completing the HIPAA Release for Third-Party Access**


The authorization form asks for information across several sections:


**Patient Information (Section 1):**


-


Patient's full legal name


-


Complete residential address


-


Telephone number


-


Date of birth


**Records Requested (Section 3):**


-


Date range of treatment (beginning and ending dates)


-


Service type checkboxes: Emergency Department, Home Care, Outpatient, Inpatient, Immunization, or Other


-


Special category initials for substance use, HIV, or mental health records


**Delivery and Recipient Details:**


-


Preferred format (Paper, CD, MyCHOP portal, Fax)


-


Law firm name and complete mailing address


-


Purpose of request (state "Legal representation" or a specific legal purpose)


-


Expiration date (default 90 days, extendable to a specified date up to one year)


**Critical for Legal Professionals:** If you need the full medical record for litigation, specify "Entire Record" on the authorization. CHOP releases an abstract by default in specified circumstances, which includes emergency records, discharge summaries, and operative reports but excludes items such as progress notes, flowsheets, and orders.


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or uninitialed sensitive categories can result in rejection or a request for correction, delaying the record request. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.

### **Preferred Communication Methods for Record Requests**


CHOP accepts requests by email and provides department-specific email addresses for record requests. When submitting by email, use a clear subject line like "Medical Record Request, \[Patient Name\]" and include your firm's contact information in the message.


For law firms handling multiple CHOP cases, managing these separate department contacts and tracking follow-ups for each gets burdensome fast. ## **Retrieving Old Medical Records from Childhood at CHOP**


### **Specific Procedures for Childhood Records**


Historical pediatric records come with their own challenges. For patients treated years ago, records may be archived and need extra processing time.


When the patient is now an adult requesting their own childhood records, they can sign the authorization themselves. For attorneys requesting records on behalf of adult clients about childhood treatment, the client signs the authorization and specifies the historical date ranges.


### **Understanding CHOP's Record Retention Policies**


Under 28 Pa. Code[§ 115.23](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/secure/pacode/data/028/chapter115/chap115toc.html) , Pennsylvania hospitals must generally keep medical records for at least 7 years after discharge. For minors, records must be kept until the patient reaches majority and then for 7 more years, or as long as adult records are maintained.


For treatment from many years ago, make the date range as specific as possible. Broad requests spanning many years can produce voluminous records and higher fees, or need extra time while staff locate archived materials.


Codes Health helps identify facilities where records may exist, which is especially valuable for cases with multiple treatment periods or incomplete client recollection of past care locations.

## **Online Access to CHOP Medical Records: Is it Possible?**


### **Registering for the MyCHOP Patient Portal**


MyCHOP provides online access to portions of the electronic health record. To register, contact the child's doctor's office to request a MyCHOP access code, then complete online registration.


Through MyCHOP, users can:


-


View test results and laboratory findings


-


Access immunization records


-


Review visit and admission summaries


-


Download appointment information


-


View medication lists


-


Access some clinical notes


### **Limitations of Online Record Access**


For legal purposes, MyCHOP has significant limitations:


-


Portal access provides only portions of the electronic medical record


-


Not all clinical documentation is available through the portal


-


File size restrictions prevent delivery of large record sets


-


Records must be viewed on a computer (not fully compatible with mobile devices)


-


Only electronically documented records can be accessed


Attorneys seeking complete records for litigation, including progress notes, nursing documentation, and full imaging studies, still need formal authorization requests to the appropriate departments.

-

-

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can I request my child's medical records from CHOP if they are over 18?**


Once a patient turns 18, they have the legal right to authorize release of their own medical records. As a parent, you'd need your adult child to sign the HIPAA authorization form, or have a power of attorney or healthcare proxy authorizing you to act for them. CHOP can't release an adult patient's records to parents without proper documentation of authority.


### **What do I do if I find an error in my child's medical records from CHOP?**


You have the right under HIPAA to request amendments. Submit a written request to CHOP's Health Information Management department explaining the specific error, with any supporting documentation. CHOP generally has 60 days to act, with a possible 30-day extension, and may accept or deny the request. If it's denied, you can submit a statement of disagreement to be included with the record.


### **Can CHOP medical records be sent directly to my attorney or another healthcare provider?**


Yes. The HIPAA authorization form includes a recipient section where you specify where records should go. Fill in the law firm or healthcare provider's name, address, and fax number, and CHOP will send records directly to the designated recipient. For legal requests, state the purpose as "Legal representation" or your specific legal purpose.


### **Are there any fees associated with requesting medical records from CHOP?**


Yes. Pennsylvania's 2026 schedule permits providers to charge up to $29.61 for search and retrieval, plus per-page copying fees of up to $2.00 per page for pages 1 to 20, $1.48 per page for pages 21 to 60, and $0.52 per page for pages 61 and beyond, with actual postage and shipping charged separately. The search and retrieval fee can't be charged when patients request their own records. When an individual is exercising the federal right of access, HIPAA's separate[cost-based fee limits](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/are-costs-authorized-by-state-fee-schedules-permitted/index.html) may control instead of the state maximums.


### **What happens if my authorization expires before CHOP processes the request?**


CHOP's MR-109 form expires 90 days after signing by default, but you can set a different expiration date up to one year from the signature date. Choosing a longer expiration on the initial form helps avoid problems if processing runs long. If you're unsure whether an expired authorization affects a pending request, confirm with CHOP's HIM department.
